source_notes: Committee list taken from https://www.ourcommons.ca/committees/en/list on 2026-09-03, session 45-1. That page groups committees as Standing Committees (25), Other Committees (1: Liaison) and Joint Committees (4: AMAD, BCAN, BILI, REGS).

Count discrepancy resolved. The brief reported the Work page filter as saying 27 standing committees and 4 joint committees. On 2026-09-03 no such sentence appears on https://www.ourcommons.ca/Committees/en/Work. Its committee filter has two groups: Committees of the House of Commons with 26 entries, and Joint Committees with 4. The 26 are the 25 standing committees plus Liaison. Standing Order 104(2) names exactly 25 standing committees, paragraphs (a) to (y), ending at Veterans Affairs. The most likely reading of 27 is 25 standing committees plus Liaison plus one of the two standing joint committees. This table carries 25 standing, Liaison, 4 joint and 13 Senate committees, 43 rows in all.

Standing Order 104(2) lists the 25 standing committees. Standing Order 104(3) names the two standing joint committees, on the Library of Parliament and for the Scrutiny of Regulations. Standing Order 107 establishes the Liaison Committee, which is a permanent committee but not a standing committee. Standing Order 108(2) gives committees the power to study all matters relating to the mandate, management and operation of the departments assigned to them, and Standing Order 108(3) sets out the special mandates of ETHI, FEWO, LANG, OGGO, PACP, PROC and SRSR. Read at https://www.ourcommons.ca/procedure/standing-orders/chap13-e.html on 2026-09-03.

Department and agency assignments for House committees are transcribed from each committee's own About page, https://www.ourcommons.ca/Committees/en/<ACRONYM>/About, all fetched and read on 2026-09-03. Where a committee's About page names a portfolio without enumerating it, the row is marked check.

AMAD and BCAN are special joint committees appointed for the current Parliament, not standing joint committees. They exist only while their order of reference stands, so re-verify them before relying on them.

Senate committee names and URLs were verified by request on 2026-09-03; all 13 returned HTTP 200 with the official title in the page title. Senate committees are assigned subject areas by the Rules of the Senate rather than departments, so the departments listed on Senate rows are an editorial mapping and every Senate row is marked check.
An empty departments array means no department is assigned to that committee under Standing Order 108(2). Its mandate is a subject area. This is the case for LANG, SRSR, LIAI, REGS and BCAN.
senate_counterpart is null on Senate and joint rows. The House rows carry the pairing, so the House-to-Senate mapping is complete when read from the House side.

The confidence field describes the committee identity and its department list, both taken from the official page. Domain assignment is editorial judgement in every row, not a published mapping, and no official source maps committees to research domains. Treat domains as a starting point for a researcher, not as authority.
No published table in Canada maps House standing committees to their assigned departments and to subject domains. This table is assembled by hand from the sources above.
